row.category: Vertical SaaS (Healthcare, Education, Real Estate, Construction, Field Service)
row.evidence: Epic publishes no pricing, and its public interface catalogue (open.epic) lists a proprietary Personnel Management web-service suite to 'create, update, and delete user records in Epic' but no SCIM interface; the specs themselves sit behind an open.epic login.
row.notes: Quote-only: Epic Systems (EHR) has no public plans or prices. Each customer runs its own Epic instance (no central endpoint), and the Personnel Management web services (user create/update/delete, user groups, login departments) are the documented user-management route; their technical spec requires an open.epic login. No SCIM interface appears in open.epic's HL7v2, FHIR, Web Services or Other catalogues, but Epic's customer docs (UserWeb) are private, so status stays unknown rather than none. No Okta OIN, Entra Learn or JumpCloud catalogue page for Epic was found at the expected URLs.

user_api.notes: Personnel Management web services; the technical spec (open.epic.com/Tech/TechSpec?spec=5453) redirects to the open.epic login. Calls go to each customer's own Epic instance.

auth.notes: Web services require a registered client ID; open.epic's FHIR page says Epic supports SMART on FHIR OAuth 2.0 and basic authentication (stated for FHIR APIs, not specifically for Personnel Management).

limitations.text: There is no central Epic endpoint; every customer runs an independent Epic instance.

fallbacks.other_sync: Personnel Management web services (proprietary user-record API)
fallbacks.notes: Epic acts as a SAML IdP for launching external apps; inbound SSO/provisioning for Epic users is not documented publicly.

citations.title: open.epic :: Web Services
citations.quote: Create, update, and delete user records in Epic. With this suite of services, you can also view and update user groups, pager IDs, user login departments, and departments the user has access to.

citations.title: open.epic :: Web Services
citations.quote: to identify the calling application as part of the Epic authorization framework.

citations.title: open.epic :: Developer Resources
citations.quote: Epic uses a federated model: every customer runs their own independent Epic instance and decides which apps can connect. There is no central Epic endpoint.

citations.title: open.epic :: Other
citations.quote: Epic supports launching an external app with SAML 2.0. The SAML 2.0 Identity Provider initiated workflow initiates from Epic, playing the SAML role of Identity Provider.

citations.title: open.epic :: FHIR
citations.quote: Epic recommends and supports the HL7 SMART on FHIR profile of OAuth 2.0, including the EHR launch and standalone launch for both patients and providers, as well as backend services. Epic also supports basic authentication.

citations.title: Epic | ...With the patient at the heart
citations.quote: We develop software that helps people get well, helps people stay well, and helps future generations be healthier.

open_questions: Whether Epic supports SCIM inbound provisioning is not documented publicly; customer documentation (UserWeb) and the Personnel Management spec require a login.
Endpoint names, auth and plan/licensing for the Personnel Management web services are not public.
Inbound SSO for Epic Hyperspace users (SAML/OIDC with a customer IdP) is not documented on open.epic.
No IdP catalogue entries were verified.
